paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD is a shepherd who takes care of ALL of you. David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." (Psalm 23:1) Grass, water, a restored soul, a path to walk. Nothing on that list is something the sheep has to earn.

And watch what happens when the road gets dark. David doesn't say the valley will never come. He says, "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me." (Psalm 23:4) The comfort isn't a shorter valley, it's who's walking next to you, and that's a better deal than any shortcut.

Then the song ends with more than David asked for. A table is set, his cup overflows, and "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever." (Psalm 23:5-6) So here's what I want you carrying out of my bakery, baker: whatever the day looks like, you belong to a shepherd who provides, who stays close, and who is taking you home. THAT is a good thing to hold onto.
